message.content:
Here’s a list of the public holidays in Canada that create long weekends (i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, or that are observed on the nearest weekday if they fall on a weekend) for the year 2023:

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Observed on (if weekend) | Long‑weekend effect |
|-------------|---------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| **January 1** (Sunday) | New Year’s Day | Monday, Jan 2 | Creates a 4‑day weekend (Sat‑Mon) |
| **January 16** (Monday) | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **February 20** (Monday) | Family Day (Ontario) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **March 20** (Friday) | Good Friday | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **April 7** (Monday) | Easter Monday (Newfoundland & Labrador, Prince Edward Island) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **May 22** (Monday) | Victoria Day (all provinces) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **June 19** (Monday) | National Indigenous Peoples Day (Northwest Territories, Nunavut) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **July 1** (Saturday) | Canada Day | Monday, July 3 | Creates a 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **September 18** (Monday) | Labour Day (all provinces) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **October 9** (Monday) | Thanksgiving (all provinces) | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **November 7** (Thursday) | Remembrance Day (observed on Thursday) | – | 3‑day weekend (Wed‑Thu‑Fri) |
| **December 25** (Monday) | Christmas Day | – | 4‑day weekend (Fri‑Mon) |
| **December 26** (Tuesday) | Boxing Day | – | 3‑day weekend (Mon‑Tue‑Wed) |

### Notes

* **Observances vary by province/territory** – some holidays (e.g., Family Day, National Indigenous Peoples Day) are only observed in certain regions.  
* **Federal holidays** (like New Year’s Day, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Remembrance Day, Christmas, Boxing Day) are observed nationwide.  
* **If a holiday falls on a weekend**, it is typically observed on the following Monday (unless otherwise specified).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need additional details!
